newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KNP BT PLAN FOR PAPER PARTNER WINS MUTED WELCOME.
newsitem.headline: KNP BT PLAN FOR PAPER PARTNER WINS MUTED WELCOME.

text.p: Dutch analysts on Friday gave a lukewarm welcome to plans by paper and packaging group KNP BT to seek a partner for its 70 percent-owned loss-making Austrian paper unit KNP Leykam.
"The whole thing is far less spectacular than it seems at first sight," MeesPierson's Wijgert Verstoep said after a company briefing for analysts.
"I see it as primarily a defensive move," said ING analyst Thibaud de Guerre. "The timing of this announcement is rather bad (given the sector situation) but KNP BT has no choice."
KNP BT said earlier it would support a partnership between KNP Leykam and paper sector rivals even if this meant a dilution of its stake.
The envisaged partnership could be anything from a joint venture to a takeover, although talk of a divestment was "highly premature", KNP BT spokesman Jan Barbas said.
"KNP Leykam cannot generate a decent return on investment alone in the medium term, so it is looking to put its own paper activities in a joint venture to reap synergy benefits," De Guerre said.
This could represent the first step in a phased divestment of the paper unit, he said.
He said a shake-out in the paper industry was inevitable. "Someone had to be the one to take the first step, and KNP BT is not a pure paper producer; it has other core activities," he said.
KNP BT is not yet in talks with any alliance candidates, but possible partners would likely be paper makers whose activities were strongly complementary, analysts said.

KNP Leykam is Europe's largest manufacturer of wood-free coated paper and a net buyer of pulp, and so would likely look to sector players who were net sellers of pulp and active in light-weight coated, De Guerre said.
"I see them going for firms long in pulp," Verstoep agreed.
"I reckon on a joint venture with a division from another company," he said, adding the Swedish paper manufacturers such as MoDo , SCA and particularly Stora appeared to be a good bet.
"The paper division isn't the whole story," he added. "KNP BT stressed today it plans further expansion in corrugated board and office products."
"More than that, it plans to take a hard line in future on activities which fail to meet its return on investment targets."
